title: Road Accident
description: Road accidents are common emergencies that can cause serious injuries and fatalities. Knowing how to respond safely at an accident scene can save lives and prevent further harm.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Road accidents involve collisions between vehicles, pedestrians, or stationary objects and can result in injuries, fatalities, and property damage. Common causes include speeding, drunk driving, distracted driving, poor road conditions, and vehicle malfunction. In India, road accidents are a major public health concern with high numbers of fatalities annually. Quick and proper response at accident scenes can significantly improve survival rates for injured victims. Understanding road accident response procedures is essential for all road users.

sections.heading: Immediate Actions
sections.content: If you witness or are involved in a road accident, first ensure your own safety before helping others. Park your vehicle safely away from the accident scene with hazard lights on. Turn off the ignition of all involved vehicles if safe to do so. Call emergency services (112) immediately and provide your location, number of vehicles involved, and severity of injuries. Do not move injured persons unless there is immediate danger from fire, explosion, or traffic. Set up warning triangles or flares if available to alert other drivers. Stay with the victims until help arrives if it is safe to do so.

sections.heading: Assessing Injuries
sections.content: Check victims for responsiveness and breathing. If a person is not breathing and has no pulse, begin CPR immediately if you are trained. Control severe bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth. Do not remove objects that are impaled in the body—stabilize them and seek medical help. Do not move victims with suspected neck or back injuries unless absolutely necessary. Keep injured persons warm and comfortable. Talk to conscious victims to reassure them and keep them calm. Note any symptoms such as confusion, chest pain, or difficulty breathing.

sections.heading: Traffic Safety at Scene
sections.content: Protect the accident scene from further collision by positioning warning devices at an adequate distance. Direct traffic around the accident if you can do so safely. Do not stand between moving vehicles and the accident scene. Turn on hazard lights of all involved vehicles. If the accident occurs at night, use flashlights to warn approaching traffic. Do not block emergency vehicle access. Keep bystanders at a safe distance to allow emergency responders to work. Follow police instructions when they arrive at the scene.

sections.heading: Legal and Documentation
sections.content: Exchange contact and insurance information with other involved parties if safe to do so. Take photographs of the accident scene, vehicle damage, and injuries if possible. Note the exact location, time, and weather conditions. Get contact information from witnesses. Do not admit fault or discuss the accident details with others except police. File a police report as required by local laws. Inform your insurance company about the accident as soon as possible. Keep all medical records and receipts related to the accident. Follow all legal requirements for reporting accidents.

sections.heading: Safety Precautions
sections.content: Never leave the scene of an accident you are involved in unless it is unsafe to stay. Do not attempt to move vehicles unless they pose an immediate danger. Do not give food or drink to injured persons as it may complicate medical treatment. Do not remove helmets from motorcycle accident victims unless they are not breathing. Always wear seatbelts and use child safety seats properly. Follow traffic rules and speed limits. Never drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Avoid distracted driving including mobile phone use. Maintain your vehicle in good condition to prevent mechanical failures. Practice defensive driving techniques.
